SEMINARS/CONFERENCE/WORKSHOPS

               I.   PRESENTATIONS

“Negotiation between home and exile in the select Novels of AbdulrazakGurnah”, A Two Day International Conference,  organized by the Department of Studies and Research in English,  School of Humanities,Pondicherry Central University, Pondicherry, 5th and 6thOctober, 2023.

Presented a paper on “ Teaching English language and Literature in Higher Education “in the ‘CONTRIBUTING Authors ‘, A Two Day conference organized by the School of Education, Christ University, Deemed to be University,  Jayanagar  Bangalore,  on 15th and 16th July.

II. INVITED LECTURES AND PANEL DISCUSSION

  1. “English language and literary studies in India: Search for new Paradigms “, organized by the Department of English,  Government College for Women, Mandya, 17th May, 2024.
  2. English language for career building,  Hindustan First Grade Collage, Mysore, 2022.
  3. Delivered A Special Lecture To MA Students Of Journalism On Building Communication And Soft Skills Through The Habit Of Reading, Organized by the Department Of Studies In Journalism , Manasagangotri, University Of Mysore, on 24 May 2025.
  4. Invited as a resource person for FDP organized by SAMPARNA EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS, Talakadu and delivered a lecture on “Teaching English language and literature”, on 19th June, 2026.
  5. Delivered a talk on “ New Trends in literary studies “ in Christ University,  Deemed to be University,  Jayanagar, Bangalore, on 15th July, 2026.

TEACHING EXPERIENCE:

  • Assistant Professor of English,VidyaVikas First Grade College, Mysore

( 24-06-2019 to 20-04-2020 )

  • Assistant Professor of English,  UG and PG Department of English, Teresian College, Mysore (August 2022 to January 2025)
  • Assistant Professor in English, ST Joseph’S College, Hassan Jesuit Educational Society, Hassan (1st Feb 2025 to 31st Aug 2025)

MASTER’S COURSES TAUGHT

  1. Nineteenth Century English Literature(core paper)
  2. Twentieth Century English Literature (core paper)
  3. Modern and Contemporary Indian English Poetry (core paper)
  4. Novels of Childhood( elective paper)
  5. Novels and the Metropolis ( 4th semester MA English)
  6. English language and Modern usage( Open Elective paper taught to PG students of MSc and MCom)
  7. Literary Criticism from Aristotle to T S Eliot ( core paper)
  8. Contemporary Literary Studies   ( core paper)
  9. The Modern Age ( core paper)
  10. New Literatures in English for III sem MA English Students. ( core paper)
  11. Cultural Studies. ( core paper)
  12. African, Australian and Canadian poetry.(core paper)
  13. Short stories in Translation
  14. Contemporary Literary Criticism. ( core paper)
  15. Business communication and soft skills. ( Open Elective paper to MSc and MCom Students)

INSTITUTION MEMBERSHIP

  1. Dhvanyaloka,  Center for English Studies and Indigenous Arts, Mysore. (Member)
  2. Mysore Literary Association ®. (Member)

ACADEMIC ENGAGEMENT &CONFERENCE CONDUCTED

CONFERENCE COORDINATION & EDITORIAL EXPERIENCE

Conference Coordinator

Two-Day National Conference on “Interdisciplinary Approaches to Contemporary Literary Studies”

Department of English (UG & PG), St. Philomena’s College (Autonomous), Mysuru

24–25 April 2026

  • Served as Conference Coordinator for the two-day National Conference.
  • Coordinated academic, administrative, and organisational activities related to the conference.
  • Assisted in coordinating communication with invited speakers, paper presenters, delegates, and the organising committee.
  • Served as Master of Ceremonies (MC) for the conference proceedings.

Editor – Conference Publication

Interdisciplinary Approaches to Contemporary Literary Studies: [Title of the Edited Volume]

Department of English, St. Philomena’s College (Autonomous), Mysuru

2026

  • Served as Editor of the conference volume arising from the National Conference.
  • Coordinated the collection, review, editing, and compilation of scholarly contributions for publication.

PERSONALSTRENTGHS:

  • Self-motivated, Confident, Hardworking and dedicated.
  • Takes initiative and works independently or as part of group.
  • Flexible to any environment.
  • Writingcritical essays on literature and Philosophy, research in English and translation works.

Quick Info:

The PG & Research Block was conceived as part of the college’s evolving mission to deepen scholarship beyond undergraduate study. After the institution’s strong foundation in undergraduate and degree programmes, the management approved postgraduate studies and a dedicated PG & Research facility to mark a new phase of academic maturity. Over time, the building and block became a hub for advanced learning, signalling the college’s transition into a centre of research culture and postgraduate excellence.

Courses and Facilities

Within this block, the college now offers a wide array of postgraduate programmes across Science, Arts, Commerce and Social Work, alongside selected doctoral research opportunities in priority disciplines. The facilities include smart‑classrooms, sophisticated laboratories, dedicated research cubicles, a seminar hall, and a resource centre aligned with modern pedagogy. Students benefit from mentorship by experienced faculty, inter‑departmental collaboration, access to e‑resources, and linkage with national/international academic networks.Facilities

Developments Over the Years:

Since its inception, the PG & Research Block has undergone continuous enhancements in infrastructure, curriculum and research output. The block has hosted numerous national and international seminars, workshops and conferences, elevating the institution’s academic profile. Laboratories and equipment have been upgraded, ICT‑enabled teaching environments introduced, and the block now supports publication initiatives, funded research projects, student research forums and collaborations with other institutions. Through these developments, the block has become the college’s landmark for postgraduate and research endeavour — embodying the institution’s ethos of Caritas in Scientia.

The Science Block stands as the academic hub of scientific learning and innovation on campus. Designed to support discovery and hands-on exploration, it houses well-equipped laboratories, research facilities, and classrooms for various science disciplines. The block provides an environment where students can experiment, analyze, and apply scientific concepts to real-world problems. With dedicated departments, modern infrastructure, and a focus on practical learning, the Science Block plays a vital role in nurturing scientific curiosity, critical thinking, and academic excellence among students.

Biology Department

The Biology Department at St. Philomena’s College offers a strong foundation in life sciences through well-structured undergraduate programs. With experienced faculty and modern laboratory facilities, the department focuses on hands-on learning, scientific inquiry, and conceptual understanding across Botany, Zoology, Microbiology, and Environmental Studies.

Key Highlights:

  • Comprehensive and industry-relevant UG curriculum

  • Well-equipped laboratories for practical and research-based learning

  • Field visits, seminars, and project-based activities

  • Supportive academic environment promoting analytical and critical thinking

  • Strong pathways for higher studies and careers in life sciences, research, and applied biological fields

The department is committed to nurturing scientific aptitude and preparing students for advanced studies, competitive exams, and diverse professional opportunities in the biological sciences.

Zoology Department

The Zoology Department provides a solid foundation in animal biology through an engaging and practical undergraduate program. Students gain hands-on experience in laboratories and field studies, developing skills in anatomy, physiology, taxonomy, and wildlife biology.

Key Highlights:

  • Comprehensive curriculum across animal diversity, genetics, ecology & physiology

  • Modern labs with specimen collections and microscopy facilities

  • Fieldwork, dissections, and student research activities

  • Focus on analytical thinking and scientific investigation

  • Strong pathways for higher studies and careers in wildlife biology, research, healthcare, and environmental management

Botany Department

  • The Botany Department at St. Philomena’s College offers a comprehensive undergraduate program focused on plant science, biodiversity, and environmental studies. With modern laboratories and experienced faculty, the department emphasizes practical learning, field exploration, and scientific research.

    Key Highlights:

    • Strong curriculum covering plant anatomy, physiology, taxonomy & ecology

    • Well-equipped labs and herbarium resources

    • Field visits, ecological studies, and project-based learning

    • Emphasis on conservation, sustainability, and research skills

    • Excellent preparation for higher studies and careers in plant science, agriculture, forestry, and environmental sectors

Physics Department

The Physics Department at St. Philomena’s College provides a rigorous undergraduate program designed to build strong conceptual and experimental foundations in classical and modern physics. With dedicated faculty and well-equipped laboratories, the department emphasizes analytical thinking, problem-solving, and hands-on practical learning.

Key Highlights:

  • Comprehensive UG curriculum covering core and applied physics

  • Modern laboratories for electronics, optics, mechanics, and advanced experiments

  • Regular seminars, workshops, and student projects

  • Focus on scientific inquiry, mathematical reasoning, and research skills

  • Strong preparation for higher studies, competitive exams, and careers in physics, engineering, and technology

The department is committed to fostering a scientific mindset and equipping students with the skills needed for academic and professional success.

Chemistry Department

  • The Chemistry Department at St. Philomena’s College offers a strong undergraduate program that blends theoretical knowledge with extensive laboratory experience. Supported by qualified faculty and modern lab facilities, the department focuses on developing a solid understanding of Organic, Inorganic, and Physical Chemistry.

    Key Highlights:

    • Well-structured UG curriculum aligned with scientific and industry needs

    • Advanced laboratories for analytical, organic, and inorganic chemistry experiments

    • Emphasis on practical skills, scientific accuracy, and safety practices

    • Student enrichment through seminars, workshops, and project work

    • Excellent preparation for higher studies and careers in research, pharmaceuticals, chemical industries, and allied fields

    The department is committed to fostering scientific curiosity, laboratory competency, and a strong foundation for future academic and professional pursuits.

St. Philomena’s college – Institution’s Innovation Council (IIC)

About IIC

The Institution’s Innovation Council (IIC) is an initiative launched by the Ministry of Education’s Innovation Cell (MIC), Government of India in the year 2018, with the objective of systematically fostering the culture of innovation, entrepreneurship, and start-up ecosystems in Higher Educational Institutions (HEIs).

The IIC framework mandates institutions to create a structured body within the campus to encourage idea generation, prototype development, innovation-based learning, start-up support, and IPR awareness among students and faculty.

The Institution’s Innovation Council (IIC) at St. Philomena’s College was established in alignment with the guidelines of the Ministry of Education’s Innovation Cell (MIC), Government of India, in the year 2024.Our goal is to foster a culture of innovation, entrepreneurship, and creativity within the campus by engaging students, faculty, and stakeholders in idea generation, incubation, and start-up activities.

Key Objectives:

  • Create an innovation-conducive environment on campus
  • Engage students and faculty in ideation, problem-solving, and start-up activities
  • Promote interdisciplinary thinking and design-driven innovation
  • Build strong linkages with industry, alumni, incubators, and funding agencies

Vision:

To create an innovative and entrepreneurial ecosystem by encouraging and creating opportunities for students, faculty to transform their business ideas into reality.

Mission:

To foster a culture of innovation, research, and entrepreneurship at St. Philomena’s College by empowering students and faculty with skills, resources, and opportunities to transform ideas into impactful solutions.

Key Initiatives

The Institution’s Innovation Council at St. Philomena’s College undertakes the following strategic initiatives throughout the academic year in line with the IIC Calendar:

  • Start-up & Entrepreneurship Events – Guiding student start-ups from concept to prototype.
  • Workshops & Seminars – Expert-led sessions on design thinking, innovation management, and business planning.
  • Celebration Activities – Observing innovation-related days such as National Innovation Day and Start-up Day.
  • Idea Competitions &Hackathons – Encouraging students to pitch and refine innovative solutions.
  • Networking Opportunities – Connecting students with successful entrepreneurs, investors, and industry mentors.

YOUTH RED CROSS

Overview

The Youth Red Cross (YRC) unit at St. Philomena’s College (Autonomous), Mysore, operates under the aegis of the Indian Red Cross Society. It is a voluntary humanitarian organization that encourages students aged 18 to 25 to engage in activities that promote health, service, and friendship. The YRC aims to instill a sense of social responsibility and humanitarian values among the youth, preparing them to respond to emergencies and contribute positively to society. 

Objectives

    • Promote Health and Hygiene: Educate students and the community about health, hygiene, and disease prevention.

    • Encourage Voluntary Service: Foster a spirit of selfless service through participation in community welfare activities.

    • Develop Leadership Skills: Provide opportunities for students to develop leadership qualities and organizational skills.

    • Disaster Preparedness: Train members in first aid and disaster response to effectively handle emergencies.

    • Promote National and International Friendship: Encourage understanding and cooperation among youth across different cultures and communities. 

Activities

The YRC unit at St. Philomena’s College has been actively involved in various initiatives, including: 

Blood Donation Camps: Organizing regular blood donation drives in collaboration with local blood banks to support patients in need.

Health Check-up Camps: Conducting general health and specialized eye check-up camps for students and the local community.

Sanitary Pad Vending Machine Launch: Promoting menstrual hygiene by installing sanitary pad vending machines on campus.

Awareness Programs: Hosting events like mime shows and seminars to raise awareness on issues such as women’s rights and harassment.

World Youth Red Cross Day Celebrations: Commemorating the day with activities that highlight the principles and mission of the Red Cross. 

Membership

Membership is open to all students of St. Philomena’s College who are interested in humanitarian service. Members are expected to actively participate in YRC activities and uphold the principles of the Red Cross. 

Contact

For more information or to become a member of the Youth Red Cross unit, please contact:

Department of Environmental Science

 

Those who protect the nature, Nature protects them.

Brief History:

The Department of Environmental Science began its journey in the year 2024 with a vision to foster environmental awareness and equip students with the knowledge and skills required to address contemporary environmental challenges. This UG programme is offered in combination with Food Science , Biotechnology , Botany and  Zoology.

Vision:

Department of Environmental Science leading with a vision of academic excellence and environmental responsibility. With a solid academic foundation and extensive experience in environmental science.

    • Transformative Education: We aim to provide an engaging and hands-on educational experience that fosters critical thinking, creativity, and problem-solving skills. Our curriculum will integrate theoretical knowledge with practical applications, enabling students to tackle real-world environmental issues.

    • Interdisciplinary Learning: Our department embraces an interdisciplinary approach, combining insights from Botany, Zoology, Food Science and Biotechnology. This holistic perspective will allow students to understand the interconnectedness of environmental systems and human impacts.

    • Active Community Engagement: We are committed to fostering strong connections between our students and the communities they serve. Through service-learning projects, internships, and collaborative research initiatives, students will apply their knowledge in meaningful ways that benefit society.

Mission:

 This program aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the interrelationships between humans and the environment, focusing on the science behind environmental processes, sustainability, and conservation.

As the world faces urgent issues such as climate change, biodiversity loss, and pollution, the Department seeks to inspire a new generation of environmental leaders who will play a pivotal role in finding solutions to these global crises. By integrating theoretical knowledge with practical application.

Innovative Initiative:

The Undergraduate Environmental Science Department is committed to shaping a sustainable future through innovative education, research, and community engagement. Our future goals focus on enhancing the academic experience, expanding research opportunities, and fostering global collaborations that empower students to become leaders in environmental stewardship.

1. Academic Developments -Designing course curriculum accordingly to the environmental issues.

2.Skills Development –Focus on developing transferable skills such as data analysis, scientific communication, and fieldwork techniques through practical sessions and laboratory work.

3.Internships-Secure internships with environmental organizations, government agencies, or private sector companies. This provides exposure to professional environments and enhances employability.

4.Fieldwork and Networks-

    • Participate in field trips that allow students to study ecosystems and conservation efforts.

    • Encourage attendance at workshops, seminars, and conferences related to environmental science. Networking with professionals in the field can lead to mentorship opportunities and job placements.

5. Diploma Course- Plans to introduce diploma course in Environmental Science with specialization in Toxicology, Environmental Technician, meteorologist and Environmental Auditors. 

Achievements:

The department is organised with well equipped laboratory and ICT enabled class room rendering focused education to the students.The department, established in 2024, has demonstrated remarkable progress by organizing workshops, field visits, seminars, and research activities within its first year. The Faculty Ms. Milagris Antonius has published book chapters in “An International Peer review  book on  Environmental Laws and Environmental Education : Book Chapter titled Environmental Engineering  and its Sustainability“ by RED`SHINE PUBLICATIONSWEDENISBN: 978-91-89764-15-6ISBN-10: 91-89764-15-3

DOI: 10.25215/9189764153DIP: 18.10.9189764153 and Book on  “Environmental Evolution ;The Process of Ecological Changes in India :Book Chapter titledBioremediation for Environmental Pollutants”SAAR Publications (Reg.) ISBN -978-81-970323-7-0.Poster presented on Nanomaterials For Environmental Remediation at International Conference on One Health : Biotechnology as a Catalyst for sustainable development(HEAL-BioTec-2023)JSS Academy of Higher Education and Research Mysuru.

Oral presentation on  A Review On Impact Of Soil Degradation On Climate Change at  international conference on CLIMATE CHANGE MITIGATION, ADAPTATION, AND RESILIENCE: A HOLISTIC APPROACH”  Department of Environmental Sciences, JSS AHER Mysuru in collaboration with National institute of Disaster Management (NIDM)

These initiatives have fostered knowledge sharing, practical learning, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Workshops focused on skill development and innovation, while field visits provided hands-on exposure to industry practices. Seminars featured experts from academia and industry, enhancing intellectual engagement. Additionally, the department has undertaken impactful research projects and built strong partnerships with other universityand local organizations to promote collaborative efforts.

View Bio

                 St. Philomena’s college established on October 9th 1946 with the benediction of His Excellency Rene Feuga MEP, the Bishop of Mysore and inaugurated with the munificence and generosity of His Highness Sri Jayachamarajendra Wodeyar, the Maharaja of the then princely state of Mysore, the first private science college in Mysore region speaks for itself volumes of its rich legacy, history and tradition.

                 Now, 79 years young, traditional programmes coexist with contemporary courses, proliferating the student strength and infrastructure. The college boasts of 27 UG depts. and 13 post graduate studies, besides, being a research centre it offers Ph.D in four disciplines with erudite scholars of outstanding calibre, gearing itself to become a Deemed to be University in the near future. From 2023 the college has begun MBA and MCA, twin premier professional courses with AICTE approval, New Delhi, yet another colourful feather on the cap of Philos. MSC Food Science and Nutrition has commenced from 2024 with ample space and infrastructure created.

                  In 2046 the college will celebrate its centenary. Hundred years down the line, the college strives in the service of nation building in providing quality education on par with global standards, that needs additional space so as to make room for evolving educational needs of our times. Therefore a prospective plan is the need of hour.  As a premier Institution of Higher Education it’s motto is Caritas in Scientia – Service through Knowledge. 

                  It strives to promote a research environment to inspire, guide, motivate, and inculcate intra-disciplinary/ multidisciplinary research culture among the faculty and students thereby its social responsibility is multifold and therefore the knowledge that students gain at Philos need to be translated into service of humanity and percolate down to mitigate suffering of millions of our countrymen who still struggle to make a decent living. 

Rev. Dr. Lourdu Prasad Joseph

M.A, B.Ed, MTh, LHE, DHE, Ph.D,(Rome)

Rector

Welcome to the St. Philomena’s Placement Cell

At St. Philomena’s College, our Placement Cell is dedicated to empowering students to achieve their career aspirations and connect with top employers. We are committed to providing comprehensive support across all our programs, including UG, PG, MBA, and MCA placements.

Brief History:

The Department of Environmental Science began its journey in the year 2024 with a vision to foster environmental awareness and equip students with the knowledge and skills required to address contemporary environmental challenges. This UG programme is offered in combination with Food Science , Biotechnology , Botany and  Zoology.

Vision:

Department of Environmental Science leading with a vision of academic excellence and environmental responsibility. With a solid academic foundation and extensive experience in environmental science.

  • Transformative Education: We aim to provide an engaging and hands-on educational experience that fosters critical thinking, creativity, and problem-solving skills. Our curriculum will integrate theoretical knowledge with practical applications, enabling students to tackle real-world environmental issues.
  • Interdisciplinary Learning: Our department embraces an interdisciplinary approach, combining insights from Botany, Zoology, Food Science and Biotechnology. This holistic perspective will allow students to understand the interconnectedness of environmental systems and human impacts.
  • Active Community Engagement: We are committed to fostering strong connections between our students and the communities they serve. Through service-learning projects, internships, and collaborative research initiatives, students will apply their knowledge in meaningful ways that benefit society.

Mission:

 This program aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the interrelationships between humans and the environment, focusing on the science behind environmental processes, sustainability, and conservation.

As the world faces urgent issues such as climate change, biodiversity loss, and pollution, the Department seeks to inspire a new generation of environmental leaders who will play a pivotal role in finding solutions to these global crises. By integrating theoretical knowledge with practical application.

Innovative Initiative:

The Undergraduate Environmental Science Department is committed to shaping a sustainable future through innovative education, research, and community engagement. Our future goals focus on enhancing the academic experience, expanding research opportunities, and fostering global collaborations that empower students to become leaders in environmental stewardship.

1. Academic Developments -Designing course curriculum accordingly to the environmental issues.

2.Skills Development –Focus on developing transferable skills such as data analysis, scientific communication, and fieldwork techniques through practical sessions and laboratory work.

3.Internships-Secure internships with environmental organizations, government agencies, or private sector companies. This provides exposure to professional environments and enhances employability.

4.Fieldwork and Networks-

  • Participate in field trips that allow students to study ecosystems and conservation efforts.
  • Encourage attendance at workshops, seminars, and conferences related to environmental science. Networking with professionals in the field can lead to mentorship opportunities and job placements.

5. Diploma Course- Plans to introduce diploma course in Environmental Science with specialisation in Toxicology, Environmental Technician, meteorologist and Environmental Auditors. 

Achievements:

content.rendered:
Two-Day International Conference on Reimagining Communication in the 21st Century: Sociological,Political, and Economic Perspectives

About the Conference

The 21st century is redefining communication, pushing the boundaries of media, politics, society, and economics. This international conference explores the sociological, political, and economic dimensions of communication in an increasingly interconnected and digitalized world. While challenges such as misinformation, media ethics, political polarization, and financial fraud pose significant risks, communication also holds transformative power, revolutionizing how societies interact, access information, and drive social change. The integration of legacy media, digital media, and artificial intelligence has democratized information access, fostering greater civic engagement, global connectivity, and economic opportunities. Social media platforms promises to empower marginalized voices, facilitate social movements, and increase public participation in governance. AI-driven innovations have enhanced data-driven decision-making, improved accessibility for differently-abled individuals and streamlined communication across industries.

By fostering cross-cultural exchanges and interdisciplinary dialogue, this conference will bridge local and global perspectives while laying the foundation for long-term collaborations in research and policymaking. Combining academic rigor with practical insights, it aims to generate actionable solutions and innovative strategies to address contemporary communication challenges. The conference will serve as a crucial platform for scholars, media professionals, and policymakers to tackle some of the most pressing global issues. Through an interdisciplinary approach, it fosters collaboration, innovation, and the development of strategies for a more informed, inclusive, and equitable digital society.

Coat of Arms – St. Philomena’s College

 

The Patron – Saint Philomena

 

Anchor: Drowning with an anchor around the neck, also the symbol of “HOPE” 

– similar to the Holy Cross symbolizing “Faith in Christ”.

Arrows: Cruel torture through an arrow.

Lillies : Purity

Palm Branch: Symbol of glorious martyrdom.

Whip: Symbol of scourge torture of criminals.- 

The way Saint Philomena was martyred

 

It is believed she was a Greek princess who became a virgin martyr and died when she was 13 years old. Remains of a young lady were discovered in May 1802 at the Catacombs of Priscilla on the Via Salaria Nova with three tiles reading “Peace be to you, Philomena.” All that is known about St. Philomena’s life comes from a Neapolitan nun’s vision. Sister Maria Luisa di Gesu claims St. Philomena came to her and told her she was the daughter of a Greek king who converted to Christianity. When Philomena was 13 years old, she took a vow of consecrated virginity. After her father took his family to Rome to make peace, Emperor Diocletian fell in love with Philomena. When she refused to marry him, she was subjected to torture. St. Philomena was scourged, drowned with an anchor attached to her, and shot with arrows. Each time she was attacked angels took to her side and healed her through prayer. Finally, the Emperor had Philomena decapitated. According to the story, her death came on a Friday at three in the afternoon, the same as Jesus. Two anchors, three arrows, a palm symbol of martyrdom, and a flower were found on the tiles in her tomb, interpreted as symbols of her martyrdom.

Devotion to Philomena began to spread once her bones were exhumed and miracles began to occur. Canon Francesco De Lucia of Mugnano del Cardinale received relics of St. Philomena and had them placed in the Church of Our Lady of Grace in Mugnano, Italy.

Soon after her relics were enshrined, cancers were cured, wounds were healed and the Miracle of Mugnano, when Venerable Pauline Jaricot was cured of a severe heart issue overnight, were all attributed to St. Philomena.

Other Saints began to venerate Philomena and attributing miracles in their lives to the young martyr, including St. John Marie Vianney and St. Peter Louis Marie Chanel.

Although controversy sometimes surrounds the truth behind St. Philomena’s life and sainthood, many believers all around the world continue to see her as a miraculous saint, canonized in 1837.

St. Philomena is the patron saint of infants, babies, and youth. She is often depicted in her youth with a flower crown, a palm of martyrdom, arrows, or an anchor.

Her feast day is celebrated on August 11.

Post Graduate Department of Food Science and Nutrition is offering M.Sc. Degree in Food Science and Nutrition from the academic year 2024-25. Since the subject has grown tremendously post Covid-19 pandemic, there is a need to train students specifically for the job market. In view of this, it was found necessary to introduce a regular course of Food Science and Nutrition at St. Philomena’s College. This program endeavors to provide students a broad-based training in Food Science and Nutrition with a solid background of basic concepts as well as exposing them to the exciting advancements in the field.

The PG Department of Food Science and Nutrition belong to St. Philomena’s college and is in PG block of the college.

Vision:

To achieve academic excellence in Food Science and Nutrition imparting in-depth knowledge to the students.Facilitating research activities and cater to the ever-changing industrial demand & societal needs.

Mission:

To provide quality education and learning experience through application of innovative teaching methods in understanding the nutrition requirements which is the basis of life and emphasize on problem solving skillsTo cultivate a culture of scientific and critical thinking and apply same in novel research.

To promote basic and advanced practical and clinical skills in conducting and interpreting laboratory investigations.To render comprehensive and quality clinical laboratory services for the betterment of community health.

Primary Goals for Postgraduate Students in Food Science and Nutrition:

 ➢Advanced Knowledge and Research Skills:

To provide in-depth understanding of food chemistry, microbiology, biotechnology, and nutrition, empowering students to engage in cutting-edge research in food safety, food processing, dietetics, and public health nutrition. 

 ➢Critical Thinking and Problem-Solving:

To cultivate analytical thinking, allowing students to identify challenges in food production, quality control, nutrition, and public health. This fosters the ability to create innovative, evidence-based solutions for complex global issues. 

 ➢Interdisciplinary Learning:

To promote a holistic educational approach by integrating principles from biology, chemistry, physics, and health sciences, helping students understand the intricate connections between food, human health, and environmental sustainability. 

 ➢Innovation in Food Technology:

To encourage creativity and innovation in food product development, food processing, and preservation. Students learn to apply food science knowledge to create new, healthier, and more sustainable food options while ensuring food safety and nutritional integrity. 

 ➢ Practical and Clinical Applications:

 To provide hands-on experiences through lab work, clinical practice, and field-based learning, allowing students to apply theoretical concepts to real-world scenarios in clinical nutrition, dietetics, and public health nutrition interventions. 

 ➢Ethical and Sustainable Practices:

To instil a deep understanding of the ethical implications of food production and nutrition, emphasizing sustainable practices that help address challenges like food security, waste reduction, and the global demand for nutritious, environmentally friendly food sources. 

 ➢Professional Development:

To enhance students’ communication, leadership, and project management skills, equipping them for impactful careers in research, the food industry, government policy, non-governmental organizations, and academia. 

 ➢Global Perspectives on Food Security:

To ensure students grasp the global challenges surrounding food security, such as climate change, population growth, and economic disparity, and how to address these issues through innovative food systems, sustainable agriculture, and nutrition policy.

 ➢Public Health Nutrition Focus:

To prepare students to design, implement, and evaluate public health nutrition programs, focusing on addressing chronic diseases, malnutrition, and health disparities across different populations, especially in underserved communities.

 ➢Collaborative and Multidisciplinary Skills:

To foster teamwork and collaborative skills by engaging students in multidisciplinary projects, enabling them to work with professionals from fields like public health, environmental sciences, and policy development.

 ➢Lifelong Learning and Adaptability:

To instil a mindset of continuous learning, ensuring that students are equipped to adapt to emerging trends in food science, nutrition, and health, and to stay ahead of developments in an ever-evolving global food landscape. This comprehensive set of goals ensures that postgraduate students not only gain advanced expertise in food science and nutrition but also develop a well-rounded skill set that prepares them to make a meaningful impact on public health, food systems, and sustainability worldwide.

➢Industrial Visits to Food Facilities:

To provide students with live exposure to the practical applications of food science and nutrition, students will participate in industrial visits to state-of-the-art food production facilities, food testing labs, and processing plants. These visits allow students to observe and engage with real-world operations, offering valuable insights into the latest technologies, production methods, and quality control measures in the food industry. 

 ➢Leading Faculty and encouraging management:

To ensure students receive the highest quality of education, the program features dynamic and interactive classes led by experienced faculty members who are experts in their fields. The faculty fosters an engaging learning environment through hands-on lab sessions, case studies, and practical demonstrations, helping students bridge the gap between theory and real-life application in food science and nutrition and encouraging them to participate in various events, conferences, summits across the world.

DEPARTMENT OF COMPUTER SCIENCE

 A Brief History:

The Department of computer science was the brain child of the computer-savvy Msgr. Fr. Leslie Moras. He was instrumental in establishing it in the year 1990 before he assumed the position of the principal of the college in 1992. He first computerized the office and then launched the courses in 1993 for the undergraduate students with the discipline of B.Sc. (CME, PMC) computer science and BA (SOCP). The department is privileged to have the students of first semester ensemble learning Computer compulsorily. Initially the Department was provided with 40 systems with the facility of Linux & Novell NetWare, later on the migrated to Microsoft windows as Computer Application was introduced for 2nd year BA, B.Sc., B.com, BBM, BSW courses. This was a purely application oriented compulsory subsidiary paper. In the year 2005, the lab was shifted to bigger premises with 48 systems. In the year 2007, the department was furnished with 5   labs and  LCD projectors of 1500 luminance. At present there are 120 systems to cater to the needs of the learners. In the year 2010, the department introduced a three years advanced diploma networking course and in the year 2012, a one year diploma in web designing. Presently computer science offers open elective courses to 2nd & 3rd year students. In the annals of the department, Fr. Leslie Moras goes in the memory lane as the sole pioneer assisted by a host of talented teachers.

Achievements:

As per the requirements of the IT industry these days, our students are trained to learn and adapt themselves to the new concepts and innovation of software and technology. This is possible for them as assignments given to them are not from the syllabus but outside the syllabus. As higher education is all about facilitating rather than mere classroom teaching, the department takes care to help the inquisitive students to develop their research skills.

Web Designing Diploma is introduced as an integrated course which helps the students to learn technologies to develop their own dynamic WebPages, which increases the employability of students. Networking is made as a part of curriculum for disciplines like commerce, management, and basic physical sciences. In collaboration with the SAP technologies, the department offers SAP course for all streams of students. 01 level and B1 level courses are also offered at an affordable price to all the students.

As an academic council member, Mr. Manuel from Infosys helps us in understanding the industrial requirements and as per his advice a paper on network security and cyber laws is included for students. An old student of St. Philomena’s college, Mr. Arun Solomon, who works as a Manager IT at L&T, Mysore, was a resource person on VMWare in a seminar organized by the department. His expertise is utilised in networking issues. Mr. Balaji from SDMIMD offered training in SPSS Software for the faculty and an additional one day workshop on the same subject was conducted by the IBM Company to facilitate the faculty. An animation course was offered free to the backward class and minority students.

National Education Policy (NEP) has been implemented from the Academic Year 2021-2022 and Revised National Education Policy(SEP)  has been implemented from the Academic Year 2024-2025.

Report on the Best Practice: Gender Equality and Impartiality at St. Philomena’s College

Introduction

St. Philomena’s College, Mysore, is deeply committed to fostering an inclusive and equitable environment where all individuals, regardless of gender, feel valued and empowered. The institution recognizes that promoting gender equality is essential for creating a harmonious and progressive academic atmosphere. As part of this commitment, the college has institutionalized the best practice of “Gender Equality and Impartiality,” involving various stakeholders through regular awareness programmes, seminars, invited talks, and competitions.

Objectives of the Practice

To promote a culture of respect, equality, and inclusion within the campus.

To raise awareness about gender-related issues and challenges.

To empower students and staff to challenge stereotypes and biases.

To engage stakeholders in constructive dialogue and activities fostering gender equality.

To create a safe and supportive campus environment for all.

Key Components of the Practice

1. Awareness Programmes

Regular awareness programmes are conducted to educate students, faculty, and staff about the importance of gender equality. These sessions include:

Gender sensitization workshops addressing unconscious biases and stereotypes.

Discussions on legal rights and protections related to gender equality.

Interactive activities emphasizing shared responsibilities and mutual respect.

2. Seminars and Invited Talks

The college organizes seminars and invited talks featuring experts from diverse fields to provide insights into gender-related issues. Topics covered include:

Women’s empowerment and leadership.

Gender-based violence and its prevention.

Breaking barriers in traditionally male- or female-dominated professions.

Mental health and gender-specific challenges.

3. Competitions

Competitions are held to engage students creatively and critically in the discourse on gender equality. Examples include:

Essay writing and poster-making competitions on themes like “Breaking Gender Stereotypes” and “Equal Opportunities for All.”

Debate competitions encouraging critical thinking on contemporary gender issues.

Cultural events highlighting the contributions of all genders to society.

4. Stakeholder Involvement

The college actively involves various stakeholders, including students, faculty, parents, and alumni, in its gender equality initiatives. Key strategies include:

Forming gender equity committees to oversee and plan activities.

Encouraging student clubs to take leadership roles in organizing events.

Partnering with NGOs and government bodies to enhance programme impact.

Implementation Strategies

Regular Scheduling: Programmes and events are planned and scheduled at the start of each academic year.

Collaborative Approach: The institution collaborates with external organizations, subject experts, and alumni to enhance the quality and reach of its initiatives.

Increased awareness and sensitivity towards gender-related issues among students and staff.

Enhanced participation of female students and staff in leadership roles within the institution.

Creation of a supportive and inclusive campus environment that encourages mutual respect and understanding.

Improved ability of students to critically analyze and address gender biases in their personal and professional lives.

Challenges Encountered

Addressing deeply ingrained societal stereotypes and biases.

Ensuring active participation from all stakeholders, especially in awareness programmes.

Balancing the academic calendar with the scheduling of gender equality activities.

Future Plans

Expanding the scope of programmes to include topics such as LGBTQ+ inclusion and intersectionality.

Organizing certificate courses on gender studies to deepen understanding.

Strengthening partnerships with organizations advocating gender equality.

Creating a dedicated Gender Equality Cell to coordinate and monitor related activities.

Conclusion

The best practice of “Gender Equality and Impartiality” at St. Philomena’s College reflects the institution’s unwavering commitment to fostering a just and inclusive environment. By engaging stakeholders through awareness programmes, seminars, invited talks, and competitions, the college ensures that its students and staff are not only informed about gender issues but also empowered to act as ambassadors of equality and impartiality. These efforts contribute to building a progressive campus culture and preparing individuals to uphold these values in their broader communities.

Report on the Best Practice: Continuous Academic Enrichment at St. Philomena’s College

Introduction

St. Philomena’s College, Mysore, is dedicated to fostering a culture of continuous learning and professional growth among its faculty members. The institution recognizes that the quality of education imparted to students is directly linked to the competency and motivation of its teaching staff. As part of its commitment to excellence, the college has institutionalized the best practice of “Continuous Academic Enrichment,” which focuses on regularly conducting Faculty Development Programmes (FDPs), Capacity Building Programmes, Orientation Programmes, and Seminars for the teaching staff.

Objectives of the Practice

To enhance the pedagogical and subject expertise of the faculty.

To equip teachers with the latest tools and techniques in teaching and research.

To foster a collaborative and innovative teaching environment.

To align faculty skills with the evolving academic and professional demands of the 21st century.

To encourage lifelong learning and self-improvement among educators.

Key Components of Continuous Academic Enrichment

1. Faculty Development Programmes (FDPs)

The college regularly organizes FDPs to help teachers stay updated with the latest developments in their respective fields. These programs cover a range of topics, including:

Innovative teaching methodologies.

Use of digital tools and technology in education.

Research methodologies and academic writing.

Interdisciplinary approaches to education.

2. Capacity Building Programmes

Capacity building initiatives are designed to enhance the leadership, organizational, and interpersonal skills of the faculty. These programmes focus on:

Effective classroom management.

Emotional intelligence and stress management.

Time management and productivity enhancement.

Building collaborative networks within and outside the institution.

3. Orientation Programmes

Newly inducted faculty members participate in structured orientation programmes to familiarize themselves with the institution’s vision, mission, and academic culture. These programmes include:

Introduction to the college’s teaching philosophy and core values.

Guidance on institutional policies and procedures.

Sessions on effective student engagement and mentoring.

4. Seminars and Workshops

Regular seminars and workshops are conducted to encourage faculty participation in discussions on contemporary academic and societal issues. Key features include:

Inviting subject matter experts and industry professionals as resource persons.

Hands-on training sessions on emerging topics like artificial intelligence, big data, and sustainable development.

Interactive sessions to exchange ideas and best practices.

Implementation Strategies

Regular Scheduling: Academic enrichment programmes are scheduled at the beginning of each academic year, ensuring all faculty members can participate.

Feedback Mechanism: Participant feedback is collected after each programme to assess its effectiveness and make necessary improvements.

Collaborative Efforts: The college collaborates with universities, research institutions, and industry partners to bring in diverse perspectives and expertise.

Resource Allocation: Adequate funding and infrastructure are allocated to support the successful implementation of these initiatives.

Impact of the Practice

Enhanced teaching quality, leading to improved student outcomes.

Increased research output and faculty participation in national and international conferences.

Greater use of technology in classrooms, making learning more interactive and engaging.

Strengthened faculty relationships, fostering a collaborative academic environment.

Better alignment of teaching methodologies with global educational standards.

Challenges Encountered

Balancing academic schedules with professional development activities.

Ensuring uniform participation across all departments.

Keeping the content of programmes relevant to the diverse academic disciplines within the college.

Future Plans

Expanding the scope of programmes to include international collaborations and exchange opportunities.

Introducing online FDPs and webinars to enhance accessibility.

Establishing a dedicated Academic Enrichment Cell to coordinate and monitor these initiatives.

Conclusion

The best practice of Continuous Academic Enrichment at St. Philomena’s College has significantly contributed to the professional growth of its faculty and the overall academic excellence of the institution. By prioritizing the continuous development of its teachers, the college not only enhances the quality of education it delivers but also reinforces its position as a leading educational institution committed to holistic learning and innovation.

Report on Institutional Distinctiveness of St. Philomena’s College, Mysore

St. Philomena’s College, Mysore, has always been at the forefront of delivering holistic education that nurtures academic excellence, personal growth, and social responsibility. The institution’s distinctiveness is reflected in its innovative initiatives, vibrant campus life, and commitment to creating a harmonious and inclusive community. Below are the key features highlighting the distinctiveness of St. Philomena’s College:

1. Teaching Life Skills as a Course

The college has integrated life skills into its curriculum, emphasizing essential abilities such as critical thinking, decision-making, emotional intelligence, and effective communication. These courses prepare students for real-life challenges and foster a sense of self-awareness and resilience. By instilling these skills, the college ensures that its graduates are not only academically proficient but also socially and emotionally competent.

2. Courses in Dance, Music, and Yoga under NEP

In alignment with the National Education Policy (NEP), the college offers diverse courses in dance, music, and yoga. These courses promote creativity, physical fitness, and mental well-being, contributing to the holistic development of students. The inclusion of such programs under NEP underscores the institution’s commitment to nurturing talents beyond conventional academics and preserving cultural heritage.

3. NSS, NCC, Rangers and Rovers, Competitive Exams, and Cultural Events

The college encourages active participation in National Service Scheme (NSS), National Cadet Corps (NCC), and Rangers and Rovers. These programs instill discipline, leadership, and a sense of social responsibility among students. Additionally, the college offers specialized training for competitive exams, ensuring that students are well-prepared for future challenges. Cultural events held on campus provide a platform for students to showcase their talents, fostering unity and cultural exchange.

4. Extensional Activities

St. Philomena’s College places a strong emphasis on experiential learning through extension activities. Students participate in visits to various institutions such as jails, milk dairies, hospitals, schools, old age homes, and forests. These visits create awareness about societal issues, promote empathy, and provide students with practical insights into different aspects of life.

5. Maintaining Eco Balance of the Campus

The college is deeply committed to environmental sustainability. Efforts to maintain ecological balance include tree plantation drives, waste management practices, and promoting biodiversity on campus. Green initiatives such as rainwater harvesting and solar energy usage reflect the institution’s dedication to preserving the environment for future generations.

6. Maintaining Peace and Amity Among Students of Different Religions

St. Philomena’s College fosters an inclusive and harmonious environment where students from diverse religious backgrounds coexist peacefully. The institution celebrates festivals and organizes interfaith dialogues to promote mutual respect and understanding. These efforts ensure that the campus remains a space for unity, tolerance, and shared growth.

Conclusion

St. Philomena’s College, Mysore, stands as a beacon of holistic education, balancing academic rigor with character building and social responsibility. The institution’s distinctiveness lies in its commitment to nurturing well-rounded individuals who are equipped to contribute positively to society. Through innovative programs and a vibrant campus culture, the college continues to inspire students to achieve their full potential while upholding values of peace, inclusivity, and sustainability.

Eco friendly campus even in the escalation in the ambit of concrete structures

1. Title of the practice: Eco friendly campus even in the escalation in the ambit of concrete structures

2. Objective of the Practice

  • To conduct an extensive environmental assessment to pinpoint and prioritize energy efficiency enhancements across our campus buildings and facilities.
  • To develop and execute a holistic waste management strategy that encompasses recycling, composting, and the proper disposal of hazardous materials, thereby reducing waste and fostering a circular economy.
  • To expand our reliance on renewable energy sources like solar panels to power up campus infrastructure, diminishing our dependence on non-renewable energy.
  • To enhance our campus greenery and landscaping to nurture biodiversity, enhance air quality, and offer serene retreats for students and staff.
  • To encourage sustainable modes of transportation, like biking, walking, and carpooling, and provide the necessary infrastructure, such as bike racks and pedestrian paths, to support these eco-friendly choices.
  • To infuse sustainability into our academic offerings, offering courses and workshops on environmental topics to enlighten students and staff about the significance of sustainability and encourage them to adopt greener practices in their daily lives.

3.The context:

In the urbanized environment of a university or college campus, the challenge of creating an eco-friendly space amidst the proliferation of concrete structures is paramount. This involves various strategies, including the development of green spaces like rooftop gardens and urban parks, which provide much-needed respite from the concrete jungle and contribute to improved air quality. Energy-efficient buildings with features like solar panels and efficient lighting reduce energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions. Sustainable transportation options such as biking, walking, and carpooling are encouraged, supported by infrastructure like bike lanes and walkways. Effective waste management practices, water conservation measures, and the promotion of biodiversity within the urban landscape are also crucial elements. Renewable energy sources like solar panels and wind turbines contribute to reducing the campus’s reliance on non-renewable energy, while environmental education and awareness campaigns foster a culture of sustainability among students and staff. Collaboration with local organizations and government agencies and a commitment to continuous improvement and innovation are essential for creating a truly eco-friendly campus.

3.The Practice:

St. Philomena’s College earmarks and standpoints as stature of the green campus are evident and discernible to illustrate the eco-friendly institution and endeavour for the sustainability of environment and promote waste management as an instrumental for global cause. The institution conducts various awareness programs to create plastic-free campus and adheres to the waste recycling.

Solid- Waste Management:Dustbins are placed in prominent places like classrooms, academic section, cafeteria, and administrative space of the institution with instructions. The wastes generated in the campus are paper, metals, dry leaves, wooden wastes, glass, wrappers, and organic wastes from canteen. The garbage pails for collection of solid wastes are located at prominent places in the campus. Our objective is to create awareness and encourage every individual in campus to be responsible and committed to be the integral part of the green campus. Plastic wastes are handed over to Mysuru City Municipal Corporation for the appropriate disposal. There is an incinerator to manage the combustion as waste treatment to burn the wastes produced in the campus. Pits are ensured timely and effectively to manage dried leaves of the campus embedded with numerous trees.

Water conservation facilities available in the Institution: Rain water harvesting Bore well /Open well recharge Construction of tanks and bunds Waste water recycling Maintenance of water bodies and distribution system in the campus.

The institution has implemented several best practices to create a greener campus. Firstly, by restricting automobile entry and promoting the use of bicycles and battery-powered vehicles, they encourage sustainable transportation options. This is complemented by pedestrian-friendly pathways that prioritize safety and eco-friendliness. Furthermore, their landscaping efforts enhance the aesthetic appeal of the campus while contributing to a greener environment. Collectively, these initiatives demonstrate a commitment to sustainability and a holistic approach to greening the campus.

5.Evidence of Success:

The institution’s endeavours to protect and enhance the environment and harness energy have yielded tangible results, supported by a series of audits and recognitions. The Green, Energy, and Environment audits have provided evidence of successful implementation of sustainable practices. This is further corroborated by the institution’s clean and green campus recognitions, which serve as external validation of their commitment to environmental stewardship. Additionally, the institution’s involvement in beyond-campus environmental promotional activities underscores their dedication to spreading awareness and influencing positive change beyond their immediate environment. These results collectively indicate the institution’s successful integration of sustainable practices and its ongoing efforts to promote environmental responsibility, both within and beyond its campus boundaries.

6.Problems Encountered and resources required: As we strive to implement sustainable practices and improve our campus environment, we have encountered several challenges along the way. One significant issue is the limited availability of financial resources to support large-scale sustainability initiatives. Additionally, changing entrenched behaviours and attitudes towards sustainability can be a daunting task, requiring significant time and effort for education and awareness campaigns. Infrastructure limitations also pose a challenge, particularly when it comes to retrofitting existing buildings with energy-efficient features or installing renewable energy systems. Moreover, coordinating efforts across various departments and stakeholders within the institution can sometimes be challenging, requiring effective communication and collaboration. To address these challenges, we require increased funding for sustainability projects, as well as additional personnel and expertise to drive implementation forward. Education and training resources are also essential to foster a culture of sustainability within our campus community. Lastly, investment in infrastructure upgrades and technology will be necessary to overcome existing limitations and achieve our sustainability goals effectively

Best Practice 1

ICT enabled teaching in conformity with technology adoption

1. Title of the practice: ICT enabled teaching in conformity with technology adoption

2. Objectives of the Practice:

  • To aim to make learning fun and captivating by using digital tools that involve students in their learning experience.
  • To make sure that all the technology we introduce is user-friendly and blends seamlessly with our current systems, making the learning journey smooth and enjoyable.
  • To implement a system that helps our staff to manage administrative tasks effectively, allowing them to focus more on supporting students and their learning experience.
  • To extend our educational reach beyond the confines of traditional classrooms, providing our students with the chance to engage and collaborate with peers across the globe.

Top of Form

  • To continuously refine the technological aspect of education based on feedback and data from students, staff, and the educational community.

3. The Context

In this era of rapid technological advancements and growing global integration, the integration of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) plays a crucial role in modern education. These goals reflect the institution’s dedication to adapting to the digital age by utilizing technology to enhance student engagement, foster collaborative learning, and streamline administrative tasks.

In this light, the necessity of ICT-based education is evident. It’s about equipping students with the skills and knowledge they need to thrive in an increasingly digital world, creating an environment that nurtures innovation, creativity, and critical thinking, and preparing the next generation of global citizens to navigate complex challenges with confidence and resilience.

These goals go beyond merely using technology; they signify a shift to a new educational model that responds to the needs of students, faculty, and the wider community. They embody a commitment to ongoing improvement and innovation, ensuring that the institution remains a leader in educational excellence in the digital age.

4. The Practice

The introduction of ICT-enabled teaching practices in the context of higher education in India marked a transformative journey, amalgamating rich traditional values with cutting-edge technological tools. This best practice aimed to redefine the educational landscape, fostering an environment where students could benefit from the best of both worlds. Uniquely tailored to the Indian higher education system, the practice emphasized the integration of technology in a way that complemented the cultural and pedagogical nuances of the region. It sought to transcend the conventional boundaries of learning by introducing tech-driven ID cards and scanners, enabling secure and efficient campus operations. E-content delivery through the Higher Education Institution (HEI) website not only streamlined access to educational resources but also aligned with India’s emphasis on digital literacy. One of the practice’s distinctive features was the incorporation of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems. This not only facilitated efficient campus management but also resonated with India’s aspiration for streamlined administrative processes in its academic institutions. The harmonization of technology with traditional values, such as harmony, peace, and morality, aimed to create a holistic educational experience reflective of India’s cultural ethos. However, the implementation of such a practice in the Indian higher education landscape was not without its share of constraints and limitations. Varied infrastructure across different institutions posed a challenge, with some facing limitations in terms of connectivity and access to the necessary technological resources. Bridging the digital literacy gap among students and faculty emerged as a priority, demanding targeted interventions to ensure a smooth transition to the tech-integrated learning environment. Resource limitations, both financial and technical, were additional hurdles. While the vision was to create an eco-friendly campus, the escalation in the ambit of concrete structures posed environmental challenges, requiring innovative solutions within budgetary constraints. The unique socio-economic fabric of India added layers of complexity, demanding a nuanced approach to address disparities and ensure equitable access to the benefits of ICT-enabled education. In conclusion, the best practice of ICT-enabled teaching in Indian higher education represented a commendable effort to blend tradition with technology. It addressed the contextual needs of the region while striving to overcome constraints through strategic interventions, aiming for a more inclusive, accessible, and technologically enriched educational experience for students across India.

5. Evidence of Success

The integration of ICT in the college environment has demonstrated notable success, enhancing various facets of operations and student engagement. Through the adoption of technology, administrative processes have become more streamlined, minimizing errors and promoting efficient management. The results of this initiative have surpassed expectations, as evidenced by improved workflow and smoother coordination across different departments. Moreover, the incorporation of ICT tools has significantly enriched the educational experience for students. The accessibility and utilization of digital resources have fostered a dynamic and interactive learning environment. This positive shift is reflected in enhanced student engagement, indicating that technology has become an integral component of the educational journey within the institution.

Furthermore, the overall feedback and reviews from both faculty and students underscore the success of these technological implementations. Faculty members express increased satisfaction with the effectiveness of digital tools in facilitating teaching and administrative tasks. Meanwhile, students appreciate the accessibility of information, collaborative opportunities, and the modernized approach to education.

6. Problems Encountered and Resources Required

Implementing ICT in the college faced challenges, including the need for extensive staff training to integrate technology effectively. Overcoming potential resistance to change emerged as another hurdle. Additionally, the initial investment in upgrading technology infrastructure posed a financial challenge. To address these issues, allocating resources for comprehensive training programs is crucial to ensure staff proficiency in utilizing ICT tools.

 In addition to that, ongoing technical support is essential to troubleshoot any issues that may arise during implementation. Adequate budget allocation for regular technology upgrades is necessary to maintain compatibility and functionality. Despite these challenges, the benefits of improved administrative efficiency and enhanced student engagement outweigh the obstacles. Therefore, a strategic investment in resources, including training, support, and budget allocation, is pivotal to the successful integration of ICT practices in the college environment.

7. Notes

For successful adoption, promote a culture of adaptability, encourage open communication, and periodically evaluate the evolving technological landscape for continuous improvement in ICT practices across institutions.

St Philomena’s Rovers and Rangers Unit

 

-:SERVICE IS OUR MOTTO:-

Introduction:

 The Bharat Scout & Guide is a voluntary, non-political, and educational movement that aims to develop young people in various aspects of their lives. This report focuses on the activities carried out by the Rover and Ranger unit of St. Philomena’s College, led by Mr. Mathew C as the Rover Leader and Dr. Sowmya as the Rangers Leader.

Purpose and Principles:

The purpose of the Bharat Scout & Guide movement is to contribute to the holistic development of young individuals, enabling them to reach their full potential physically, intellectually, emotionally, socially, and spiritually. The movement follows the purpose, principles, and methods established by Lord Baden Powell in 1907. It emphasizes inclusivity, welcoming young people from all backgrounds, irrespective of their origin, race, or creed.

Composition of the Unit:

The Rover and Ranger unit of St. Philomena’s College comprises a total of 30 students, with 18 rovers and 12 rangers. The unit provides a platform for these young individuals to engage in meaningful activities, develop essential life skills, and contribute to their communities.

International Cultural Jamboree:

In the academic year 2021-22, the Rangers and Rovers from St. Philomena’s College had the opportunity to participate in the International Cultural Jamboree held at Moodbidre. This event provided a unique cultural exchange platform for young people from different countries, promoting understanding, friendship, and global citizenship.

Organizing Health Camps:

The unit actively engages in organizing health camps, recognizing the significance of physical well-being. These health camps aim to raise awareness about various health issues, promote preventive measures, and provide basic healthcare services to the underprivileged. Through these initiatives, the students learn about healthcare systems and develop empathy and compassion for those in need.

Blood Donation Camps:

St. Philomena’s College unit of the Bharat Scout & Guide also actively participates in blood donation camps. By encouraging students to donate blood, the unit helps address the constant demand for blood in hospitals and supports life-saving treatments. This activity not only instills a sense of responsibility and altruism but also raises awareness about the importance of blood donation within the college community.

Cleanup Drive on World Environment Day:

To commemorate World Environment Day, the Rover and Ranger unit organizes a cleanup drive. This initiative aims to create awareness about environmental issues, such as pollution and waste management. By actively participating in the cleanup drive, students contribute to the local community’s cleanliness, fostering a sense of responsibility towards the environment.

Special Invited Talks:

The unit arranges special invited talks for students to inculcate values and develop essential skills. These talks provide a platform for experts and experienced individuals to share their knowledge, experiences, and insights. By exposing the students to diverse perspectives, the talks help broaden their horizons, enhance their understanding of various subjects, and inspire them to become responsible citizens.

Conclusion:

 The Bharat Scout & Guide unit at St. Philomena’s College, led by Mr. Mathew C, the Rover Leader and Dr. Sowmya, the Ranger Leader, have been actively engaged in promoting the holistic development of young individuals. Through their participation in international events, health camps, blood donation drives, cleanup activities, and special invited talks, the students have gained valuable experiences, skills, and values. These initiatives contribute to their growth as responsible citizens.

Auditorium Design Essentials

Architectural Layout & Space Planning

  • Seating Capacity & Space Allocation: Allocate approximately 18 square feet per person to accommodate seating, aisles, and technical areas.

  • Floor Design: Consider tiered or sloped flooring to enhance sightlines and audience engagement. 

  • Seating Arrangements: Choose from various layouts like proscenium, thrust, or arena, depending on the intended use and audience experience.

Integrated Acoustic and AV Design for Optimal Auditorium Performance

Acoustics & Sound Management

  • Acoustic Treatments: Incorporate acoustic panels, diffusers, and specialized ceiling and wall treatments to ensure clear and evenly distributed sound throughout the auditorium.

  • Sound Isolation: Design spaces to prevent sound leakage between different areas, maintaining acoustic integrity.

Audio-Visual & Lighting Systems

  • Lighting: Implement adequate and adjustable lighting systems to cater to various events and moods.

  • Visual Displays: Equip the auditorium with robust visual display systems, including projectors and screens, to enhance presentations and performances.

Inclusive and Ergonomic Auditorium Design

Accessibility & Safety

  • ADA Compliance: Ensure the design includes accessible entrances, seating areas, and restrooms to accommodate individuals with disabilities.

  • Safety Codes: Adhere to fire safety regulations, including appropriate row spacing and clear passageways, to ensure the safety of all occupants. 

Seating Comfort & Ergonomics

  • Seat Dimensions: Design seats with adequate width and spacing to provide comfort during extended events.

  • Row Spacing: Maintain sufficient distance between rows to allow easy movement and enhance comfort.

Ms.Juhie Singh
Women’s Cell Coordinator

ANTI-RAGGING COMMITTEE

 

St. Philomena’s Degree College (Autonomous) Mysore is committed in fostering a safe and inclusive learning environment for all its students. In pursuit of this commitment, the college has established an Anti-Ragging Committee to ensure the well-being of students and to create a campus culture that promotes respect, tolerance, and camaraderie.

PRIMARY OBJECTIVE

 
  • Prevention of Ragging:To create awareness and prevent incidents of ragging within the campus.
  • Education and Sensitization: To educate students about the consequences of ragging and sensitize them to the impact it can have on victims.
  • Prompt Action: To promptly address any reported cases of ragging and take appropriate action against the perpetrators.

ANTI-RAGGING COMMITTEE FUNCTIONS

 
  • Orientation Programs: Conducting orientation programs at the beginning of each academic year to educate students about the college’s policies on ragging.
  • Awareness Campaigns: Organizing awareness campaigns throughout the year to emphasize the importance of maintaining a ragging-free environment.
  • Grievance Redressal: Providing a platform for students to report incidents of ragging and ensuring that prompt and appropriate action is taken.
  • Counselling and Support: Offering support and counselling services to victims of ragging and taking steps to rehabilitate them.
  • Regular Monitoring: Regularly monitoring different areas of the campus, especially during the initial days of the academic year, to prevent any potential incidents of ragging.
  • Action Against Offenders: The Anti-Ragging Committee is empowered to take strict disciplinary action against any individual or group found guilty of ragging, in accordance with the college’s policies and the laws of the land.

The Anti-Ragging Committee at St. Philomena’s Degree College (Autonomous) Mysore plays a pivotal role in creating a safe and nurturing environment for all students. By fostering a culture of respect and empathy, the committee contributes to the overall well-being and academic success of our students. We encourage everyone in the college community to actively support and participate in maintaining a ragging-free campus.

content.rendered:
Vision is a journey to the destination and mission is the path. Dharma is the lifetime endeavor and day to day activities constitute the karma. The narratives may sound different but the ultimate aim is the ‘good of humanity’ for an education institution. The distinctiveness of St. Philomena‘s College is the experience of the people in the campus and the calibre of the graduates. The feasibility of realizing the vision is the collective responsibility of the management, staff, students, the alumni and the parents. Concerted efforts are put in  to sustain the bonding among the various stakeholders. In keeping with the exigencies of the time there is an operative system in place to ensure the core values of the institution quality-based education without any distinction:

With the open admission policy, opportunity is created for the aspiring young people to empower themselves in a diverse setting. Before the pandemic restrictions around the world, heterogeneity among the students was rich. At a time there were students from more than 30 countries, mainly developing nations and girl students from highly orthodox background students from almost all the states of India especially the north-eastern states remote regions of India from Tibetan settlements, farmers’ children, poor students from the locality as well as students from well-off families both financially and educationally.

The institution attracts people of diverse background because of the prevailing conducive atmosphere of the campus and the inclusive mindset of the management and staff. The parents are confident that their wards receive good education and come out as confident, global citizens. Teaching not just from books but with the life experience;

Education has a vital campus component as well as significant social aspect. With the available opportunities both these components need to be balanced.

And applicable and all encompassing curriculum, delivered in a blended mode by team of competent teaching faculty is ensured. The assignments, projects, debates, situation and case study analysis are all with the social dimension. By creating awareness about the social scenario the young people are bound to form a mindset which will reflect in their life and actions

 The diverse background of the students and the prevailing unique culture and humanity in the campus and with healthy interactions and mutual respect students pick up the best from the other.
